exposure: COVID-19 epidemic (time period: March-December 2020 vs. March-December 2019)
outcome: Rates of large for gestational age (LGA)
Rates of small for gestational age (SGA)
cohort: The cohort consisted of 847 women diagnosed with gestational diabetes (GDM) who attended a university hospital diabetes clinic in Slovenia, comparing those treated during the COVID-19 epidemic (March-December 2020, n=417) with those treated in the same period a year prior (2019, n=430).
finding: During the COVID-19 epidemic, women with GDM were diagnosed earlier, had higher fasting glucose, and achieved lower HbA1c compared to the previous year, yet the epidemic did not result in worse glucose control during pregnancy or worse maternal and perinatal outcomes in Slovenia.
mod_finding: No significant differences in pregnancy outcomes, which included caesarean section rates, were observed between the COVID-19 epidemic and pre-epidemic periods.
